 // Move cursor\n116\tawait out.write(blockData);               // Write sequentially\n117\t```\n118\t\n119\t**Problems:**\n120\t- Still sequential — blocks arriving out of order are written in arrival order\n121\t- Concurrent block completions would race on the cursor position\n122\t- No atomic positional guarantees\n123\t\n124\t### What `createSyncAccessHandle` Provides\n125\t\n126\t**Correct implementation:**\n127\t```typescript\n128\tconst handle = await fileHandle.createSyncAccessHandle();\n129\t\n130\t// Atomic positional writes, regardless of arrival order:\n131\thandle.write(blockData, {at: blockIndex * blockSize});\n132\t\n133\t// No cursor races — each write is independent\n134\t```\n135\t\n136\t---\n137\t\n138\t## Architectural Impact\n139\t\n140\t### Current Data Flow (INCORRECT)\n141\t\n142\t```\n143\tGE Decoder (worker) → decoded block (192 KB)\n144\t                    ↓\n145\t            FileSystemWritableFileStream (main thread?)\n146\t                    ↓\n147\t              Sequential append (WRONG for out-of-order!)\n148\t```\n149\t\n150\t### Required Data Flow (CORRECT per §6.2)\n151\t\n152\t```\n153\tGE Decoder (worker) → decoded block (192 KB)\n154\t                    ↓\n155\t            OPFS Worker (separate thread per §6.2)\n156\t                    ↓\n157\t      createSyncAccessHandle.write(buf, {at: blockIndex * blockSize})\n158\t                    ↓\n159\t              Correct positional write\n160\t```\n161\t\n162\t### Thread Violation\n163\t\n164\t**Current:** `FileSystemWritableFileStream` typically used on main thread\n165\t**Required:** `createSyncAccessHandle` is **worker-only**\n166\t\n167\tThe current implementation either:\n168\t1. Uses a suboptimal API even in a worker (can use `createSyncAccessHandle` instead)\n170\t\n171\t---\n172\t\n173\t## Block Transfer Scenarios\n174\t\n175\t### Scenario 1: Normal Sequential Arrival\n176\t```\n177\tBlocks arrive: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5...\n178\tBoth APIs work (but createSyncAccessHandle is still required per §6.2)\n179\t```\n180\t\n181\t### Scenario 2: Repair Code (Missing Blocks)\n182\t```\n183\tMissing blocks: 3, 7, 15\n184\tRepair transmission sends: [3], [7], [15]\n185\t❌ FileSystemWritableFileStream: Writes sequentially → file scrambled\n186\t✅ createSyncAccessHandle: write(buf, {at: 3*size}) → correct\n187\t```\n188\t\n189\t### Scenario 3: Resume from Interruption\n190\t```\n191\tCompleted blocks: 0-999 (bitmap shows this)\n192\tResuming from: block 1000\n193\tBlocks arrive: 1000, 1005, 1002, 1010, 1001... Objective\n32\t\n33\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n34\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n35\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n36\t>\n37\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n38\t\n39\t- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n40\t  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n41\t- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n42\t- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n43\t- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n44\t\n45\t### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n46\t\n47\tMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\n48\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n49\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n50\t\n51\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n52\t|---|---|---|---|\n53\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n54\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n55\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n56\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n57\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n58\t\n59\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n60\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n61\t> one would overstate throughput.\n62\t\n63\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n64\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n65\t\n66\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n67\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n68\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n69\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## 2. Glossary\n74\t\n75\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n76\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n77\tplan they mean exactly this:\n78\t\n79\t| Term | Meaning here |\n80\t|---|---|\n81\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n82\t| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n83\t| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n84\t| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n85\t| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n86\t| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n87\t| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n88\t| **Beacon** | A special frame carrying file-level metadata instead of payload (D17, §7.2). |\n89\t| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n90\t| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n91\t| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n92\t| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n93\t| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n94\t| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n95\t| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n96\t| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n97\t| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t\n101\t## 3. What multi-gigabyte breaks, and the fix\n102\t\n103\tFour assumptions in the pre-multi-GB design do not survive contact with a 4 GB file.\n104\t\n105\t### 3.1 The fountain decoder does not scale — in TIME, not memory\n106\t\n107\tThis is the correction the plan review surfaced, and it matters because the first\n108\tversion of this section got it half right.\n109\t\n110\tD5 chose an LT code with a **Gaussian elimination** decoder, verified at\n111\t[`sim/`](../research/sim/). GE costs O(K²) in *memory* and O(K³) in *bit operations*.\n112\tThe original block-layer decision sized K from the memory term alone and concluded 4 MB\n113\tblocks (K = 16,384) were fine because the coefficient matrix is only 32 MB.\n114\t\n115\t**The memory term was never the binding constraint. Time is.**\n116\t\n117\tEach arriving packet is reduced against up to `rank` stored pivot rows; each row\n118\toperation XORs the coefficient mask (K/8 bytes) *and* the payload (L bytes). Reaching\n119\tfull rank costs `W = 2 · (K²/2) · (K/8 + L) = K² · (K/8 + L)` bytes of memory traffic,\n120\tand the block only lasts `K·L / R` seconds at wire rate R — so the decoder must\n121\t**sustain**:\n122\t\n123\t```\n124\trequired = W / (K·L/R) = K · (K/8 + L) · R / L    bytes/sec\n125\t```\n126\t\n127\t> The leading factor is **1, not 2** — the 2 and the /2 in `W` cancel. {"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_202608021550369a04f0f2357542f7","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"glm-4.7","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_35549b8ab2c54ff1a5f7c1b4","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/coding/screenferry/docs/notes/bf-60mq-positional-write-interface.md","content":"# Positional Write Interface Design (bf-60mq)\n\n## Overview\n\nDesign a positional write interface that mirrors the worker-side OPFS `createSyncAccessHandle` API, enabling out-of-order block writes without buffering. This is critical for repair/resume scenarios where blocks arrive out of sequence.\n\n## Requirements\n\n### Functional Requirements\n\n1. **Positional writes**: `write(buf, {at})` method that writes to specific file offsets\n2. **Order independence**: Writes must not depend on arrival order\n3. **No buffering**: Interface should not require in-memory buffering of blocks\n4. **OPFS compatibility**: Must work with worker-side `createSyncAccessHandle` semantics\n5. **Type safety**: TypeScript interfaces with clear type definitions\n\n### Non-Functional Requirements\n\n1. **Performance**: Minimal overhead for write operations\n2. **Error handling**: Graceful handling of write failures, quota exhaustion\n3. **State compatibility**: Must integrate with existing receiver session states\n\n## API Design\n\n### Core Interface\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Positional write handle for out-of-order block writes.\n *\n * Mirrors worker-side OPFS createSyncAccessHandle semantics with\n * write(buf, {at}) capability for repair/resume scenarios.\n */\nexport interface PositionalWriteHandle {\n  /**\n   * Write data at a specific file offset.\n   *\n   * @param buffer - Data to write\n   * @param options - Write options including position\n   * @returns Promise resolving to bytes written\n   * @throws WriteError if quota exceeded or I/O error occurs\n   */\n  write(buffer: Uint8Array, options: WriteOptions): Promise<number>;\n\n  /**\n   * Close the handle and flush all writes.\n   *\n   * @returns Promise resolving when closed\n   */\n  close(): Promise<void>;\n\n  /**\n   * Get current file size.\n   *\n   * @returns Promise resolving to file size in bytes\n   */\n  getSize(): Promise<number>;\n\n  /**\n   * Flush writes to disk (optional, for checkpointing).\n   *\n   * @returns Promise resolving when flushed\n   */\n  flush?: () => Promise<void>;\n}\n\n/**\n * Write options for positional writes.\n */\nexport interface WriteOptions {\n  /**\n   * File offset in bytes where write should begin.\n   * Must be non-negative.\n   */\n  at: number;\n\n  /**\n   * Optional flag to truncate file at this position.\n   * If true, file is truncated to `at` bytes after write.\n   */\n  truncate?: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Write error with code and context.\n */\nexport class WriteError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    public code: 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED' | 'IO_ERROR' | 'INVALID_OFFSET' | 'HANDLE_CLOSED',\n    message: string,\n    public context: {\n      offset?: number;\n      bytesAttempted?: number;\n      cause?: Error;\n    }\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'WriteError';\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Factory Interface\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Factory for creating positional write handles.\n */\nexport interface PositionalWriteHandleFactory {\n  /**\n   * Create a new positional write handle for a file.\n   *\n   * @param filePath - Virtual path within OPFS\n   * @param expectedSize - Expected final file size (for pre-allocation)\n   * @returns Promise resolving to write handle\n   */\n  createHandle(\n    filePath: string,\n    expectedSize: number\n  ): Promise<PositionalWriteHandle>;\n\n  /**\n   * Reopen an existing file for positional writes.\n   *\n   * Used during resume to re-establish handle to partial output.\n   *\n   * @param filePath - Virtual path within OPFS\n   * @returns Promise resolving to write handle\n   */\n  reopenHandle(\n    filePath: string\n  ): Promise<PositionalWriteHandle>;\n}\n```\n\n## Implementation Architecture\n\n### Layer 1: Abstraction Layer\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Abstraction over different write backends.\n */\ninterface WriteBackend {\n  write(buffer: Uint8Array, offset: number): Promise<number>;\n  close(): Promise<void>;\n  getSize(): Promise<number>;\n}\n```\n\n### Layer 2: OPFS Backend (Primary)\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * OPFS backend using createSyncAccessHandle (worker context).\n *\n * This is the primary backend for out-of-order writes.\n */\nclass OPFSWriteBackend implements WriteBackend {\n  private fileHandle: FileSystemFileHandle;\n  private syncHandle: FileSystemSyncAccessHandle | null = null;\n  private closed = false;\n\n  constructor(fileHandle: FileSystemFileHandle) {\n    this.fileHandle = fileHandle;\n  }\n\n  async write(buffer: Uint8Array, offset: number): Promise<number> {\n    if (this.closed) {\n      throw new WriteError(\n        'HANDLE_CLOSED',\n        'Cannot write to closed handle',\n        { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length }\n      );\n    }\n\n    if (!this.syncHandle) {\n      this.syncHandle = await this.fileHandle.createSyncAccessHandle();\n    }\n\n    try {\n      // Positional write using sync handle\n      this.syncHandle.write(buffer, { at: offset });\n      return buffer.length;\n    } catch (e) {\n      if (e instanceof Error && e.name === 'QuotaExceededError') {\n        throw new WriteError(\n          'QUOTA_EXCEEDED',\n          'Storage quota exceeded',\n          { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length, cause: e }\n        );\n      }\n      throw new WriteError(\n        'IO_ERROR',\n        `Write failed: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`,\n        { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length, cause: e instanceof Error ? e : undefined }\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    if (this.syncHandle) {\n      this.syncHandle.close();\n      this.syncHandle = null;\n    }\n    this.closed = true;\n  }\n\n  async getSize(): Promise<number> {\n    const file = await this.fileHandle.getFile();\n    return file.size;\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Layer 2: FileSystemWritableFileStream Backend (Fallback)\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Fallback backend using FileSystemWritableFileStream.\n *\n * Used when createSyncAccessHandle is unavailable (main thread).\n * Requires seek() which may not be supported in all browsers.\n */\nclass StreamWriteBackend implements WriteBackend {\n  private writable: FileSystemWritableFileStream | null = null;\n  private closed = false;\n  private currentOffset = 0;\n\n  async open(fileHandle: FileSystemFileHandle): Promise<void> {\n    this.writable = await fileHandle.createWritable();\n    this.currentOffset = 0;\n  }\n\n  async write(buffer: Uint8Array, offset: number): Promise<number> {\n    if (this.closed || !this.writable) {\n      throw new WriteError(\n        'HANDLE_CLOSED',\n        'Cannot write to closed handle',\n        { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length }\n      );\n    }\n\n    try {\n      // Seek to position (if supported)\n      if (offset !== this.currentOffset) {\n        await this.writable.seek(offset);\n        this.currentOffset = offset;\n      }\n\n      // Write data\n      await this.writable.write(buffer);\n      this.currentOffset += buffer.length;\n      return buffer.length;\n    } catch (e) {\n      throw new WriteError(\n        'IO_ERROR',\n        `Write failed: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`,\n        { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length, cause: e instanceof Error ? e : undefined }\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    if (this.writable) {\n      await this.writable.close();\n      this.writable = null;\n    }\n    this.closed = true;\n  }\n\n  async getSize(): Promise<number> {\n    if (!this.writable) {\n      throw new WriteError('HANDLE_CLOSED', 'Handle is closed', {});\n    }\n    // Note: WritableStream doesn't expose size directly\n    // This may need alternative implementation\n    throw new Error('getSize() not supported on Stream backend');\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Integration with Receiver States\n\n### Modified ReceivingState\n\n```typescript\nexport interface ReceivingState extends BaseRecvState {\n  type: 'receiving';\n  active: {\n    blockIndex: number;\n    pivots: Map<number, GERow>;\n    rank: number;\n    consecutiveHigher: number;\n    switchThreshold: number;\n  } | null;\n  \n  // NEW: Use positional write handle instead of stream\n  out: PositionalWriteHandle | null;\n  \n  manifest: BlockHashManifest | null;\n  stats: {\n    fps: number;\n    cameraPxPerModule: number;\n    packetsPerSec: number;\n    eta: number;\n    dutyCycle: number;\n  };\n}\n```\n\n### Block Write Logic\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Write a decoded block to its correct position.\n *\n * @param handle - Positional write handle\n * @param blockData - Decoded block data\n * @param blockIndex - Block index (determines offset)\n * @param blockSize - Block size from beacon\n */\nasync function writeBlock(\n  handle: PositionalWriteHandle,\n  blockData: Uint8Array,\n  blockIndex: number,\n  blockSize: number\n): Promise<void> {\n  const offset = blockIndex * blockSize;\n  \n  // Write at specific offset - order independent!\n  await handle.write(blockData, { at: offset });\n}\n```\n\n## Usage Example\n\n### Main Thread This is critical for repair/resume scenarios where blocks arrive out of sequence.\n\n## Requirements\n\n### Functional Requirements\n\n1. **Positional writes**: `write(buf, {at})` method that writes to specific file offsets\n2. **Order independence**: Writes must not depend on arrival order\n3. **No buffering**: Interface should not require in-memory buffering of blocks\n4. **OPFS compatibility**: Must work with worker-side `createSyncAccessHandle` semantics\n5. **Type safety**: TypeScript interfaces with clear type definitions\n\n### Non-Functional Requirements\n\n1. **Performance**: Minimal overhead for write operations\n2. **Error handling**: Graceful handling of write failures, quota exhaustion\n3. **State compatibility**: Must integrate with existing receiver session states\n\n## API Design\n\n### Core Interface\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Positional write handle for out-of-order block writes.\n *\n * Mirrors worker-side OPFS createSyncAccessHandle semantics with\n * write(buf, {at}) capability for repair/resume scenarios.\n */\nexport interface PositionalWriteHandle {\n  /**\n   * Write data at a specific file offset.\n   *\n   * @param buffer - Data to write\n   * @param options - Write options including position\n   * @returns Promise resolving to bytes written\n   * @throws WriteError if quota exceeded or I/O error occurs\n   */\n  write(buffer: Uint8Array, options: WriteOptions): Promise<number>;\n\n  /**\n   * Close the handle and flush all writes.\n   *\n   * @returns Promise resolving when closed\n   */\n  close(): Promise<void>;\n\n  /**\n   * Get current file size.\n   *\n   * @returns Promise resolving to file size in bytes\n   */\n  getSize(): Promise<number>;\n\n  /**\n   * Flush writes to disk (optional, for checkpointing).\n   *\n   * @returns Promise resolving when flushed\n   */\n  flush?: () => Promise<void>;\n}\n\n/**\n * Write options for positional writes.\n */\nexport interface WriteOptions {\n  /**\n   * File offset in bytes where write should begin.\n   * Must be non-negative.\n   */\n  at: number;\n\n  /**\n   * Optional flag to truncate file at this position.\n   * If true, file is truncated to `at` bytes after write.\n   */\n  truncate?: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Write error with code and context.\n */\nexport class WriteError extends Error {\n  constructor(\n    public code: 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED' | 'IO_ERROR' | 'INVALID_OFFSET' | 'HANDLE_CLOSED',\n    message: string,\n    public context: {\n      offset?: number;\n      bytesAttempted?: number;\n      cause?: Error;\n    }\n  ) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'WriteError';\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Factory Interface\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Factory for creating positional write handles.\n */\nexport interface PositionalWriteHandleFactory {\n  /**\n   * Create a new positional write handle for a file.\n   *\n   * @param filePath - Virtual path within OPFS\n   * @param expectedSize - Expected final file size getSize(): Promise<number>;\n}\n```\n\n### Layer 2: OPFS Backend (Primary)\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * OPFS backend using createSyncAccessHandle (worker context).\n *\n * This is the primary backend for out-of-order writes.\n */\nclass OPFSWriteBackend implements WriteBackend {\n  private fileHandle: FileSystemFileHandle;\n  private syncHandle: FileSystemSyncAccessHandle | null = null;\n  private closed = false;\n\n  constructor(fileHandle: FileSystemFileHandle) {\n    this.fileHandle = fileHandle;\n  }\n\n  async write(buffer: Uint8Array, offset: number): Promise<number> {\n    if (this.closed) {\n      throw new WriteError(\n        'HANDLE_CLOSED',\n        'Cannot write to closed handle',\n        { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length }\n      );\n    }\n\n    if (!this.syncHandle) {\n      this.syncHandle = await this.fileHandle.createSyncAccessHandle();\n    }\n\n    try {\n      // Positional write using sync handle\n      this.syncHandle.write(buffer, { at: offset });\n      return buffer.length;\n    } catch (e) {\n      if (e instanceof Error && e.name === 'QuotaExceededError') {\n        throw new WriteError(\n          'QUOTA_EXCEEDED',\n          'Storage quota exceeded',\n          { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length, cause: e }\n        );\n      }\n      throw new WriteError(\n        'IO_ERROR',\n        `Write failed: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`,\n        { offset, bytesAttempted: buffer.length, cause: e instanceof Error ? e : undefined }\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    if (this.syncHandle) {\n      this.syncHandle.close();\n      this.syncHandle = null;\n    }\n    this.closed = true;\n  }\n\n  async getSize(): Promise<number> {\n    const file = await this.fileHandle.getFile();\n    return file.size;\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Layer 2: FileSystemWritableFileStream Backend (Fallback)\n\n```typescript\n/**\n * Fallback backend using
